sources.title: Conference networking made simple, in three short videos
sources.description:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03678-9

Working the room is a skill you can practise and prepare for. Here’s how.

sources.title: First observation of a giant star swallowing its neighbour
sources.description:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03784-8

Finding provides new insights into what happens within stellar mergers — plus, using quantum physics to securely pinpoint someone’s location.

sources.title: How to make AI data centres more sustainable
sources.description:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03708-6

Tech companies and governments face opposition over data centres’ expansion, in part because of their huge power requirements. They must not be powered with fossil fuels.

sources.title: Microbiome home tests are taking off. Can they be trusted?
sources.description:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03710-y

Our reporter mailed off her poo to find out what two companies say about her microbiome. Here’s what she found.

sources.title: Kings of the jungle? This early human had surprising survival skills that rivalled ours
sources.description:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03777-7

Teeth found in south China challenge the idea that Homo erectus was limited to woodlands and savannahs.

sources.title: Intra-stellar: a star inside a giant star
sources.description:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03273-y

Long-term monitoring of a giant star in the Andromeda galaxy reveals, for the first time, the decay of the orbit of another star inside the giant’s envelope.

sources.title: Glucose-powered implant brings devices for treating diabetes a step closer
sources.description:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03377-5

A device that stimulates the main nerve between the brain and the internal organs when blood sugar is high is an effective therapy in rat models of diabetes.

sources.title: Poxviruses probably evolved in the digestive system of animals
sources.description:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03436-x

Large and giant DNA viruses that infect unicellular eukaryotes are abundant in the environment but have rarely been found in the gut microbiome. The discovery of such viruses that prevail in the digestive system of humans and animals exposes a long-overlooked facet of the gut microbiome that clarifies the origin of poxviruses.

sources.title: Meet ‘egoviruses’: the surprise microbes living in the guts of millions of people
sources.description:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03766-w

Egoviruses could be the evolutionary missing link between giant viruses that infect single-celled organisms and those that can infect people.

sources.title: A new view of Amazonian leaf seasonality
sources.description:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03490-5

Much of the Amazon rainforest was thought to be evergreen, but high-resolution satellite imagery reveals that many of its trees can remain leafless for longer than expected.

sources.title: Are you a budding science sleuth? Take our plagiarism quiz to test your skills
sources.description:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03040-z

Sleuths and publishers seize on ‘tortured phrases’ to detect research fraud. Sometimes they can raise a smile.

sources.title: AI must be held accountable — value statements won’t protect human dignity
sources.description:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03717-5

Technology companies can’t be the judges of their own regulatory compliance. Centuries of history explain why.

sources.title: A grant to hand out more grants — and build a research area
sources.description:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03689-6

A rapid microgrants scheme called the Field Building Accelerator aims to launch new scientific fields.

sources.title: Quantum physics can prove where you are
sources.description:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03378-4

Demonstrating your location to someone far away is surprisingly hard. Quantum correlations offer a way to do so without needing to trust any quantum hardware.

sources.title: The right to do wrong
sources.description:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03517-x

An equal chance.

sources.title: Widespread deciduousness reveals diverse Amazonian phenological strategies
sources.description:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11284-y

A basin-wide assessment of Amazonian deciduousness using high-resolution satellite observations shows a diverse range of phenological strategies across the Amazon rainforest, contrary to the prevailing view of Amazonian phenology.

sources.title: A glucose-powered artificial neuroimmune axis for metabolic control
sources.description:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11251-7

NeuroAxis restores glucose tolerance, improves insulin sensitivity and normalizes glycaemic control, with therapeutic effects persisting after treatment cessation in rat models of type 1 and type 2 diabetes.

sources.title: Rainforest adaptation in late Homo erectus from southern China
sources.description:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11155-6

Eight Homo erectus teeth from two caves in southern China reveal that the species persisted in closed rainforest ecosystems between 324 and 184 ka, challenging assumptions about their ecological preferences and behavioural limitations.

sources.title: An inspiral of a star inside a common envelope with its giant companion
sources.description:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11221-z

Observations of AT 2025abao provide direct evidence of common-envelope inspiral, revealing frictional energy dissipation and constraining how orbital energy drives stellar-envelope ejection during binary evolution.

sources.title: Evidence for late Middle Pleistocene Homo erectus in mainland East Asia
sources.description:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11271-3

Late Middle Pleistocene hominin teeth from the Naxian and Baxian caves of southern China, dated to around 324–184 thousand years ago, fill a gap in the geographical and chronological distribution of Homo erectus in East Asia.

sources.title: Closest relatives of poxviruses prevail in human and animal guts worldwide
sources.description:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11283-z

A diversified group of DNA viruses with large linear genomes is discovered, egoviruses, that comprise a putative viral order most closely related to animal-infecting poxviruses, and prevail in the animal digestive system.
